title: A Change at a Damascus School Has Syrians Reading the Runes
hook: A century after opening as a bastion of secularism, Damascus's prestigious Laique school has mandated sex-segregated classrooms, prompting Syrians to debate what the shift signals about their society's future.

title: How Italy's guiltiest food ritual went public
hook: Once frowned upon in polite dining rooms as an unrefined habit of the working class, 'fare la scarpetta'—wiping the plate clean with bread—has evolved into an Italian badge of culinary honor.

title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
hook: In the late 19th century, visitors to the Maine woods encountered French-Canadian lumberjacks with a bizarre condition that made them involuntarily leap, echo commands, and strike out at the slightest startle.

title: Ivan the Terrible Wanted to Marry Elizabeth I. How Did England's 'Virgin Queen' Reject the Russian Czar Without Souring Trade Relations?
hook: When Ivan the Terrible proposed marriage to Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen faced a delicate geopolitical dilemma: turning down a volatile autocrat without tanking England's lucrative Russian trade.

title: Why did Stalin commit a robbery? The bloody heist that made the dictator’s name
hook: Long before ruling the Soviet Union, a young Stalin made his name by orchestrating a brazen, blood-soaked 1907 bank heist in Tiflis to bankroll the Bolshevik revolution.

title: Chinese Scam Boss Murdered in Sri Lanka Had Multiple Identities
hook: The brazen abduction and murder of a Chinese cybercrime syndicate leader in Sri Lanka reveals the network of shadow identities that enabled his cross-border scam operations.

title: Leaked files reveal how Deloitte Cyprus helped Roman Abramovich hide $10B fortune
hook: Leaked financial records expose how accounting giant Deloitte's Cyprus office backdated records and shuffled assets to help Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich shield a $10 billion fortune from sanctions.

title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
hook: In a stunning cybersecurity twist, federal investigators allege that executives at corporate ransomware negotiation firms were covertly operating the extortion infrastructure used by the ShinyHunters hacking ring.

title: An Ancient Virus Explains Why the Human Brain Is Special
hook: Millions of years ago, a prehistoric retrovirus silenced key brain-development genes across primate lineages, leaving ancestral humans uniquely untouched and altering our evolutionary trajectory.

title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
hook: After artificial intelligence produced a proof for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, human mathematicians finally unpacked its internal logic—revealing profound insights for number theory.

title: Ken Paxton Says He’s Tough on Crime. His Trust Invested $600,000 in a Convicted Fraudster’s Company.
hook: While campaigning on an unbending tough-on-crime platform, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton saw his blind trust quietly sink $600,000 into a venture founded by a convicted fraudster.

title: Traction!
hook: Friction is rarely noticed until it fails, but tribologists study how this ubiquitous contact force quietly governs everything from continental drift to microscopic machinery.

title: Mohammed Massoud Morsi on Writing About Palestinian Lives Beyond the Headlines
hook: Author Mohammed Massoud Morsi explores how literature can restore humanity and complexity to Palestinian life, creating space for personal narratives that transcend bleak headline statistics.

title: The rejuvenating secrets of the immortal jellyfish
hook: When injured, starved, or dying of old age, the tiny jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii pulls off nature's ultimate reversal: transforming its mature cells back into youthful polyps to live all over again.

title: Pompeii wasn’t destroyed when you think it was
hook: For centuries, textbooks dated the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius to August 24, AD 79, but emerging archaeological evidence—from charcoal graffiti to autumnal harvests—points to an entirely different month.

title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)
hook: Published in 1677 without a single word of text, the enigmatic Mutus Liber attempted to guide initiates through the creation of the Philosopher’s Stone solely through cryptic, allegorical engravings.

title: Kremlin payment firm A7 has been pumping billions in ‘untraceable’ cash into global financial system
hook: Leaked banking records show how sanctioned payment firm A7 hauled over 280 tons of physical banknotes from Moscow markets to covertly pump billions into global finance.

title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
hook: British regulators have cracked down on Cryptomus, a shapeshifting payment processor unmasked as a critical laundering hub for international ransomware syndicates and dark web cartels.

title: Sanctioned Investor in Cambodian Scam Compound Owns California Mansion
hook: Even after being sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury for financing notorious cyber-scam compound operations in Cambodia, an international investor still holds a pristine $5 million mansion in California.

title: How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy?
hook: Biologist Toby Kiers reveals how underground fungal networks function like sophisticated market traders, exchanging carbon and phosphorus with plant roots through ruthless biological haggling.

title: ‘It’s magic’: scientists rediscover how to make ancient Roman colour-changing glass
hook: Materials scientists have finally solved the 1,600-year-old riddle of the Roman Lycurgus Cup, reverse-engineering the ancient nanotech recipe that allows the glass chalice to shift color under light.

title: For the First Time, Scientists Trapped an Elusive Antimatter Particle—and Contained It for Months. It Could Allow Them to Test an Enduring Physics Theory
hook: Physicists have succeeded in trapping elusive antimatter particles for months at a time, opening the door to experiments that could finally explain why our matter-filled universe exists at all.

title: Horrible, unmanly, indispensable
hook: When firearms first spread across Renaissance Italy, knights and humanists decried them as unmanly 'devil's work'—until the brutal math of gunpowder warfare forced a total cultural surrender.

title: The Dominican Baseball Factory
hook: This hard-hitting investigation exposes the predatory shadow economy behind Major League Baseball in the Dominican Republic, where street-level scouts and moneylenders prey on prospects as young as 11.

title: Canada's ghost island where guests still check in
hook: On a subarctic island off the coast of Labrador, an abandoned 19th-century salt cod hub has been preserved in amber, letting modern travelers stay in a remote ghost village cut off from modern life.

title: From Sisi’s Satirist to Sisi’s Guest: Bassem Youssef’s Surprise Appearance
hook: The unexpected reappearance of satirist Bassem Youssef at Egypt Forum 2026 highlights the complicated, shifting dance between political dissent, celebrity, and state power in the Arab world.

title: Inside the world's last divided capital
hook: Cleaved in two since 1974, Nicosia's UN buffer zone remains an eerie time capsule where retro car dealerships and bullet-scarred buildings sit undisturbed in no-man's-land.

title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
hook: A court sentencing reveals how an active-duty U.S. soldier hacked into major telecom providers to steal metadata from over 100 million mobile customers and ransom the records.

title: US Court Orders Lebanese Ex-Minister to Pay $35M in Torture and Fraud Case
hook: A U.S. federal court ordered a former Lebanese government minister and his associates to pay $35 million for a chilling conspiracy involving business fraud and underground detention.

title: Data brokers have detailed files on you. Here’s what’s in them — and how it impacts you
hook: When everyday consumers requested their secret profiles from data brokers, the files exposed how corporations trade sensitive dossiers tracking everything from alcohol consumption to medical habits.

title: Were Two Ancient Chinese Astronomers Beheaded for Failing to Predict an Eclipse in 2134 B.C.E.? The Story May Be a Myth, but It Underscores the Real Risks of Interpreting Celestial Events
hook: Investigates the 4,000-year-old Chinese legend of royal court astronomers allegedly executed for drunkenly failing to predict an eclipse, separating myth from ancient political realities.

title: The Marquis de Lafayette's Brother-in-Law Participated in Three Revolutionary Wars, Supporting American Independence but Brutally Suppressing an Uprising by Enslaved Africans in Haiti
hook: The Marquis de Lafayette’s brother-in-law fought for freedom at Yorktown and renounced his titles in France, only to turn around and violently crush slave rebellions in Saint-Domingue.

title: The Vikings had a terrifying myth about the end of the world. Was it inspired by a real deadly disaster?
hook: Historical researchers suggest the terrifying Norse myth of Fimbulwinter—three consecutive summers without sun preceding the end of the world—preserves memories of catastrophic 6th-century volcanic eruptions.

title: “Earth Not a Globe”: Parallax’s Zetetic Astronomy (1865)
hook: Meet Samuel Rowbotham, the Victorian eccentric whose 1865 pseudoscientific canal experiments and theatrical debates single-handedly launched the modern flat-Earth movement.

title: A Saudi on the Silent Fear of the Houthi Strikes
hook: A Saudi writer offers a rare, candid glimpse into the private anxieties gripping Riyadh and Dammam as strikes hit home, contrasting official silence with the street-level mood.

title: Nuclear Weapons Waste Made Workers Sick. Despite a Law Meant to Help, the DOE Keeps Fighting Their Claims.
hook: An investigation exposes how the Department of Energy systematically fights compensation claims filed by sick nuclear weapons workers, evading a law designed explicitly to help them.

title: Where to See the World’s Creepiest Dolls and Toys
hook: Delve into the eerie history of the 18th century when improved manufacturing techniques turned children's playthings into the world's creepiest dolls.

title: He was a pirate, slaver and killer. So why is he England's national hero?
hook: Examine the dual legacy of Sir Francis Drake, an Elizabethan national hero who was simultaneously a brutal pirate and slave trader.

title: The duchess charged with treason and witchcraft
hook: Uncover the chilling 15th-century trial of Eleanor Cobham, a duchess charged with treason and witchcraft in a politically charged medieval showdown.

title: 'Pretty Boy' Floyd, One of the Most Notorious Outlaws of the Great Depression, Was Shot and Killed in an FBI Raid 92 Years Ago
hook: Relive the dramatic final moments of Great Depression outlaw 'Pretty Boy' Floyd, who was gunned down in an FBI raid 92 years ago.

title: During the American Revolution, the City of Lancaster, Pennsylvania, Served as the United States' Capital for Just One Day
hook: Discover how Lancaster, Pennsylvania, served as the capital of the United States for precisely one chaotic day during the American Revolution.

title: Smugglers Collected Up to $509M on Europe Routes in 2025
hook: Investigate how smugglers collected up to $509 million along European trafficking routes in a single year.

title: Sri Lanka Records Zero Prosecutions Amid Online Scam Surge
hook: An eye-opening look at how Sri Lankan police detained over 1,000 foreign cyber-scam suspects only to be thwarted by an outdated legal code.

title: New US law requires dating apps to include warnings on romance scams
hook: A new U.S. law forces dating apps to issue explicit warnings if a user has been banned for operating a romance scam.

title: A nanoparticle revealed the tiny impact of a single gas atom
hook: Physicists have successfully isolated the minuscule force exerted by a single gas atom using a specialized nanoparticle.

title: Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering
hook: Witness stunning microscopic imagery capturing the malaria parasite in the exact act of breaking into human red blood cells.

title: ‘You’re Not Supposed To Be Here’
hook: An intimate long-form exploration of how Palestinian citizens of Israel navigate escalating marginalization and racism in the wake of shifting political tides.

title: Syria’s Winemakers Press on Under New Alcohol Rules
hook: A fascinating look at a resilient group of Syrian winemakers preserving a centuries-old craft amidst economic hardship and changing regulations.

title: Arthur Conan Doyle Based Sherlock Holmes on a Real-Life Scottish Surgeon Who Used Deduction to Diagnose Patients and Investigate Crimes
hook: Before Sherlock Holmes existed on paper, Scottish surgeon Dr. Joseph Bell dazzled students by deducing complete strangers' occupations and criminal histories simply by glancing at their coats and gait.

title: From Flights to ‘Incentives,’ Indonesian Nickel Giant Harita Approved Payments for Local Politicians and Leaders
hook: Leaked internal records reveal how Indonesian mining giant Harita funnelled hundreds of thousands of dollars into covert payouts for local politicians and community leaders to secure its nickel empire.

title: How Hungary’s richest man funneled millions into Orbán’s propaganda machine
hook: An investigation traces how Viktor Orbán's childhood friend and Hungary's wealthiest tycoon channeled over $13 million in state contract wealth into an online propaganda engine.

title: After Millions in Stolen SNAP Benefits, Trump Administration Moves to Fight Theft
hook: After sophisticated skimming crews looted millions in food assistance directly from vulnerable families' EBT cards, federal authorities are finally overhauling outdated security standards.

title: Why Washing Machines Took Decades to Catch On
hook: Though electric washing machines promised to eliminate the most backbreaking household chore, early manufacturers spent decades fighting deep-seated social taboos before families would buy one.

title: Mystery of Roman sarcophagus unearthed at Westminster Abbey solved at last, expert says
hook: An inscribed Roman coffin unearthed outside Westminster Abbey baffled historians for years—until new archaeological evidence revealed it had been brazenly recycled by an 11th-century abbot.

title: Anatomy Unzipped: John of Arderne’s Sweden Scroll (ca. 1425–35)
hook: In a 15th-century English medical scroll, surgeon John of Arderne illustrated human anatomy through bizarre, surreal drawings of patients prying their own bodies open for inspection.

title: The endurance of Earth’s hidden alpine glaciers
hook: While the world's surface glaciers retreat, massive 'rock glaciers' shielded under blankets of mountain debris are quietly surviving, offering unexpected hydrological lifelines to high-altitude ecosystems.

title: See Inside Cells Like Never Before in These Vivid Microscopic Images
hook: The latest winners of the Nikon Small World competition reveal the astonishing, alien architecture inside living cells through cutting-edge microscopic imaging techniques.

title: Astronomers Detect the Oldest Known Fast Radio Burst, Spewed From an Ancient Galaxy Just Three Billion Years After the Big Bang
hook: Astronomers have intercepted a powerful fast radio burst that traveled across space since the universe was just three billion years old, offering a rare glimpse into the primordial cosmos.

title: How to be a (Roman) man
hook: Historian Catharine Edwards explores how Cicero and Roman moralists defined true masculinity not through bravado or dominance, but through a rigorous and agonizing public theater of self-restraint.

title: Yemen’s Salafist Commanders Are Shaping Its Battlefield
hook: A report on how three Salafist scholars transformed their religious preaching networks into powerful military brigades that are reshaping Yemen's battlefields and political future.

title: In Company Style: Illustrations from James Skinner’s Kitāb-i tashrīḥ al-aqvām (1825)
hook: Commissioned in 1825 by an Anglo-Indian cavalry officer, this lavish Persian manuscript offers an extraordinary illustrated window into the crafts, customs, and religious communities of late Mughal India.

title: Dogs, devils, clams and catfish: When cancer is contagious
hook: In Tasmanian devils, domestic dogs, and ocean clams, cancer cells have broken the ultimate biological rule by turning into infectious, contagious pathogens that spread from host to host.

title: The Norwegian island that wanted to abolish time
hook: On the Arctic island of Sommarøy, where the sun doesn't set for over two months each summer, residents launched a spirited campaign to officially throw out the clock and become the world's first time-free zone.

title: Why Was Adolf Hitler Obsessed With Vermeer’s The Astronomer?
hook: Hitler viewed Vermeer's 'The Astronomer' as the pinnacle of Aryan artistic genius, leading Nazi looters on an obsessive mission to seize it for his planned master museum.

title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
hook: Erasmus called them 'little moons' while critics condemned them as chaotic clutter, but Renaissance poet Philip Sidney wielded the humble parenthesis as an art form.

title: This Social Worker Was Supposed to Help Orphans Find Homes. Instead, She Abducted Children Who Already Had Families and Sold Them for Profit
hook: Posing as a compassionate social worker, Georgia Tann orchestrated the abduction of over 5,000 children from poor families to sell them to wealthy clients in a decades-long adoption racket.

title: New documents show how a retail chain’s sales practices helped put guns on US streets
hook: Unsealed legal records expose how a major Midwestern retail chain ignored glaring red flags to sell firearms that directly supplied street violence and violent crimes.

title: Groups Associated With India’s Far-Right Receive Millions Through US Donor-Advised Funds
hook: Bellingcat tracks how millions of dollars in tax-deductible American philanthropic funds were quietly channeled through donor-advised accounts to organizations tied to India's far right.

title: Have scientists finally found a way to save the banana from disaster?
hook: With Panama disease pushing the world's ubiquitous Cavendish banana toward collapse, geneticists and breeders may have finally engineered a viable path to save the crop.

title: Was van Gogh’s ‘The Starry Night’ a flight of fancy or a real sky?
hook: Astronomers cross-referenced historical planetary data with meteorology to argue that Vincent van Gogh’s swirling sky in 'The Starry Night' was modeled on a specific July night in 1889.

title: A Texas Cop Signed on to Help ICE Deport His Neighbors. It Tore the Town Apart.
hook: When a small-town Texas police officer partnered with federal immigration agents to deport local residents, it unraveled community trust and tore a close-knit municipality in two.

title: The French Far Right Has Opened Pangram’s Box
hook: When an anonymous tip alleged that one of France's celebrated literary sensations was generated by AI, it ignited an existential brawl exposing the literary world's entanglement with far-right culture wars.
